source_snapshot.procedure: For always-off, always-on and previous: enter BIOS, set policy through OOB IPMI, inspect chassis status, Discard Changes and Reset, re-enter BIOS and compare AC Loss Control; source also clears logs and embeds root/0penBmc.
source_snapshot.criteria: BIOS AC Loss Control status should match IPMI-OOB setting.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; changes only always-off, exposes password through `-P`, greps Last Power Event and leaves BIOS comparison to an operator.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; correctly requires all three policies, protected credentials, independent configured-policy readback, operator BIOS evidence, per-step approval and baseline restoration without implying physical AC removal.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly recognizes the operator boundary but covers only one policy and confuses a historical event with configured policy state.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Case-specific controls, classification and hybrid execution boundary are technically sound and retained.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant or earlier completed record; the next row is a distinct functional G3 behavior test.
historical_reviews.v3_1: This row compares BMC policy configuration with BIOS display; it does not itself require a physical AC-loss event, while every policy write and reboot remains approval-gated and baseline-restored.

original_test_intent: For each always-off, always-on and previous policy, verify that the configured BMC/IPMI power-restore policy is represented by the matching BIOS AC Loss Control value, then restore the recorded baseline.
original_method: In an approved maintenance window, bind one SUT/BMC, capture baseline policy and BIOS value, apply one approved policy at a time through protected OOB access, independently read back the configured policy, reboot under operator control, capture the BIOS display, compare against the owner mapping, and restore/verify baseline.
manual_activity: The owner approves the target, mapping, maintenance window and each mutation/reboot. An operator enters BIOS, captures AC Loss Control after each policy and confirms final baseline restoration.
required_inputs: Protected BMC credentials and supported LANPlus/cipher path
Owner-approved mapping among always-off, always-on, previous and BIOS labels
Recorded baseline policy and BIOS value
Timeout, unreachable-host recovery and baseline-restoration runbook
safety_requirements: Obtain explicit approval before every policy write and reboot
Never use embedded default credentials or expose passwords on argv/logs
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Do not treat Last Power Event as configured-policy readback
Stop on set/readback/BIOS mismatch, unreachable target or unsafe workload
Do not perform physical AC removal under this row
Restore and independently verify baseline before release
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only target and baseline prechecks
After explicit approval, set exactly one named policy through the protected path
Capture set response and independent configured-policy readback
Coordinate one approved reboot and operator BIOS capture
Compare only using the owner-approved mapping
Stop on any mismatch and assist approved recovery
Restore and verify baseline only with explicit approval
engineer_actions: Approve target, mapping, policy order and each mutation/reboot
Provide secure access and recovery path
Confirm baseline restoration and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The always-off write is only one-third of source coverage, `-P` exposes secrets, and Last Power Event is not the configured policy. The BIOS operator boundary is valid.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use an approved secret-safe IPMI path to set one of all three policies only after confirmation, query the actual configured System Power Restore Policy, then coordinate operator BIOS comparison and baseline restoration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All three policies, Discard Changes and Reset/re-entry flow, BIOS comparison and 30/30-minute estimates remain; log clearing and fixed credentials are prohibited.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a three-row evidence matrix containing approved policy, pre-state, protected set result, independent configured-policy readback, reboot/session identity, BIOS displayed value, comparison, and restoration status.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secret-safe access, exact target binding, per-step approval, configured-policy rather than event readback, stop conditions and baseline restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: It intentionally excludes actual G3 behavior; the adjacent functional AC-loss case owns controlled physical-cycle validation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A failed write, reboot or restoration can alter post-outage recovery or availability; BIOS label mapping is platform-specific.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported vendor/Redfish policy interface only with approved semantic equivalence and recorded original/actual method. Each of all three source policies remains separately evidenced; one successful policy cannot stand for the others.
expected_evidence: Redacted SUT/BMC/BIOS identity, maintenance approval and baseline
For each policy: approval, protected set response and actual configured-policy readback
For each policy: reboot/session identity, operator BIOS capture and match/mismatch
Baseline restoration/readback, reachability, preserved events and engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require matching the three OOB power policies to BIOS AC Loss Control. Unsafe fixed credentials and log clearing are rejected controls, not conflicting semantic targets.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The hybrid comparison is executable once the target, owner mapping, protected credentials, operator, approvals and recovery plan are supplied.

review_improvement: Preserves the three-policy BIOS comparison while preventing one-policy reduction, event/policy confusion, credential exposure and failure to restore the baseline.
independent_technical_reasoning: `Last Power Event` describes history, not the configured restore policy, so it cannot prove the value shown in BIOS. The minimal valid evidence chain is policy write, configured-policy readback, reboot-bound BIOS observation and restoration for each enumerated policy; actual G3 behavior is separate coverage.
